sections.overview: Psychrolutes phrictus, the blob sculpin, is a deep-water sculpin in the family Psychrolutidae.
sections.identification: Its head and body carry many small cirri, and the skin is loose; the Chinese-language Taiwan Fish Database also notes that the fins can be partly hidden beneath it.
sections.habitat: It is a bathydemersal fish of the North Pacific, reported from Japan and the Bering Sea south to California, at about five hundred to two thousand eight hundred metres.
sections.diet: FishBase reports sea pens, crabs and molluscs among its prey.
sections.behavior: A research record from the eastern Pacific documents a specimen collected over muddy bottom at about one thousand one hundred metres; few behavioral observations are available.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not provide a detailed account of its reproduction.
sections.ecology: Its congener P. marcidus is instead known from temperate Australian waters, at a shallower reported depth range of six hundred to one thousand two hundred metres.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports no IUCN assessment for this species.
